newsitem.title: UK: David S. Smith hit by stg, Europe economies.
newsitem.headline: David S. Smith hit by stg, Europe economies.

text.p: British packaging and paper firm David S. Smith (Holdings) Plc said on Wednesday the strength of sterling and the weakness of continental European currencies continues to affect the company's performance.

"The group faces a difficult and challenging period ahead," chairman Alan Clements said in a statement. "Nonetheless we are confident that the many strengths of the group will see us through the current adversity and that we have a good future".

The group reported a 23 percent drop in pre-tax profits to 96.0 million pounds ($160.9 million) for the year to May 3, down from 124.6 million in the previous year. Turnover fell 4.5 percent to 1,180 million pounds while the dividend for the year was raised by 6.7 percent to 8.0 pence per share.

"The cautious outlook we have held for some considerable time has been fully warranted," said Clements. "The fall in operating profit was...mainly due to the effect of the rapid appreciation of sterling on the selling price of paper".

In the second half of the year, sterling rose around 25 percent against other European currencies which meant that UK prices effectively climbed by 25 percent. This made the UK very attractive to the group's French and German competitors, and "rapidly" brought down UK prices, particularly for paper.

"If sterling stays at the current level it will take a considerable time for our cost structures to adjust to the competitive realities of the present exchange rate and the process will be painful," Clements added.

He added it was also essential for the group's fortunes that there be a "sustained period of reasonable growth" in European economies. Around one quarter of the group's operating profit now originates in France and other European countries. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
